Multi-line progress reports appeared on the estimate issue and one had to be reformatted by hand, while a missing `watchdog/estimate-issue` made the cron post nothing at all, silently. The speed tier was switched three times by patching the deployed PATH shim with an `assert old in s` against a 90-character substring, and the main TUI never received the tier because its launcher exec'd an absolute codex path. Diagnosis: every number the owner stated lived in several places at once - a message, a cap file, a goal text, a script literal - and no component had one accessor for it; the estimate issue had no single writer; the shim had no committed source of truth. Fix: `local/bin/run_mode.py` validates one briefing into `watchdog/run-mode.json`, derives the cap files (never empty, never non-numeric, an unreadable one being unknown rather than zero), regenerates the shim from the committed template and refuses a hand-edited one with a diff; `estimate_post.py` renders the two-line estimate and refuses any other body; `ready_report.py` posts the hourly readiness report with each ready-but-open PR's reason read from daemon state; `full-speed-mode.md`, `main.md` (Standing reports) and `issues-prs.md` 6.1 carry the rules, and the retired inbox #26 is swept to #500. Lesson: a number the owner states once must have exactly one home and exactly one accessor - a second copy is wrong within the hour, and a channel with more than one writer drifts back to prose.
- **Nothing measured the limit and nothing noticed the dead endpoint (W3).** Symptom: 69 sessions died in an hour against a primary endpoint that had been answering 503 the whole time, and the rest died above the second key's real concurrency limit; the caps were chased by hand through ten values and the pause/resume round trip saved zeros it could not parse back. Diagnosis: the caps were operator opinion written into three files, with no measurement underneath them and no per-endpoint health at all, so every correction was a guess made after the deaths. Fix: `local/bin/capacity_controller.py` is the only writer of the cap files - additive increase after a full quiet window at saturation, multiplicative decrease on the first refusal of a window, per-endpoint attribution from the structured `failure_class`/`endpoint` fields, three `endpoint_5xx` deaths inside 120 s tripping the account to cap 0, recovery through a single half-open read-only probe, and the measured limit carried into the next run's seed. Lesson: a ceiling the owner states is a ceiling, never a target; the number that matters has to be measured, and an endpoint with no health check is an endpoint that fails silently for an hour.
- **The operator layer lived in /tmp and disagreed with itself (W4).** Symptom: four pause variants, two owner-say revisions, two launchers and two estimate copies existed only in `/tmp` and `~/bin`; one pause script had wiped the crontab with a `sed` delimiter bug; the speed switch asserted an exact 90-character substring of a generated file; and the goal keeper resumed the goal five minutes after the owner's terminal stop order. Diagnosis: there was no deployment step, so every fix was a copy and every copy was a fork, and the message channel had no way to express "this message does not resume". Fix: one versioned `install.sh` with a hash manifest that refuses to overwrite a hand patch and offers `--verify` as the daemon's start gate; one `owner-pause.sh` whose every phase is clamped to the briefed deadline and which releases queued dispatches through `watchdog/drain` rather than killing them; one `owner-resume.sh` that restores only from the recorded state and checks every precondition first; one `owner-say.sh` whose `terminal` mode writes `watchdog/goal-hold` before the message. Lesson: a script with no installer has no version, and a stop order needs a mechanism, not a convention.
- **The merge path was a /tmp script with timer-based failure markers (W5).** Symptom: ready PRs sat open; the daemon's `pr<N>.failed` markers were bare touch files with a two-hour backoff, so one systemic lane failure blocked every affected PR for two hours; PAR was a constant; three lane-runner revisions were hand-patched during the run; and the lane carried a fallback push with `MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1`. Diagnosis: a failure with no class can only be handled by a timer, and a timer cannot tell a conflict that is still there from one a merge of main already resolved. Fix: `merge-daemon.sh`, `merge.sh`, `daemon-scan.py`, `daemon.conf`, `lane.sh` and `worktree_resolve.sh` land in the repository; the marker becomes a JSON record with a class, a reason and an attempt count that clears on an observable change (a new head, a finished repair, a conflict that no longer reproduces, a newer installed release); PAR is computed from nproc, load and free slots each loop; and the hook-skipping fallback push is deleted. Lesson: a backoff is what you use when you have no observation - every marker should name the thing that would clear it.
- **The run's debris was cleared by hand, by date glob and by digit filter (W6).** Symptom: sessions killed by the provider were re-dispatched in hand-built waves; parked lanes were repaired by an operator reading `needs-attention` files; four PRs whose content was already on main stayed open; twenty stale lane directories were swept with globs that would have deleted live state on a different day. Diagnosis: nothing owned the state a failed run leaves behind, so the cleanup was improvised each time and the improvisation selected by filename rather than by record. Fix: `local/bin/janitor.sh` is one idempotent sweep of five passes selecting by record field only - re-dispatching a session that ended in a transient class under a per-(PR, role, head) budget and never one that ended clean, repairing `merge`/`build` lanes through committed briefs and `fix-lane.sh`, closing a PR only when its three-dot diff against main is empty AND its head is an ancestor of main, dropping lane state whose PR is closed, and expiring dispatch spool entries past the run's cutoff. Lesson: a cleanup that selects on a filename is a cleanup that will one day delete live work.
- **Two one-host fixes: the union driver and the import closure (W7).** Symptom: nearly every merge conflicted on the append-only telemetry logs until a union merge driver was written into one host's `.git/info/attributes`, where it protects exactly one checkout; and separately, two modules outside the umbrella import closure had no `.olean` after `lake build`, so every lane's per-file pre-push gate failed three hours into the run. Diagnosis: both fixes were correct and neither was committed, so neither existed for anyone else; and nothing checked reachability at the time a module was added, which is the only cheap moment to check it. Fix: a committed `.gitattributes` carries the union driver and `worktree-setup.sh` asserts it on every bootstrap; `scripts/check_umbrella_imports.py` runs inside the existing `local-ci/build` step, names each unreachable module with its exact import line and re-export file, and never edits a re-export file. Five older orphans found on the head this landed on keep the step `--warn-only` under issue 551. Lesson: a fix that lives in one host's git config is a fix the project does not have.
- **Three defects appeared only when the seven items were built as one tree (integration).** Symptom: with all seven items applied, seven `test_run_mode` cases and one `test_install_owner_tools` case failed, although each item's suite had passed on its own. Diagnosis: (1) `run_mode.render_shim` knew two rendering positions for the speed tier and the committed shim template that landed with it uses a third, its anchored `SPEED_ARGS=` line, so `set speed` would have rewritten the exec line instead and produced a shim `install.sh` had never released; (2) `run_mode.controller_path` resolved `capacity_controller.py` next to itself while the controller resolves its policy under `MIPSTARRE_REPO_ROOT`, so tool and data could come from two roots and every pause in a temporary root exited 3; (3) the crontab test asserted "no /tmp in the install path" as a proxy for "installed from a file under the cache root", which is false on a host whose TMPDIR is /tmp. Fix: `render_shim` rewrites the anchored `SPEED_ARGS=` line and its output is now byte-identical to `install.sh` in both directions, and `apply_speed` calls `install.sh --record codex` so the daemon's `--verify` start gate stays green after a speed change; `controller_path` resolves under `repo_root()`; the two test assertions now check the invariants themselves. Lesson: items with disjoint file sets still share contracts, and a contract that is only written in an integration note is a contract nothing tests.
- **A fourth integration defect: the pause/resume round trip reproduced the failure it was built to fix.** Symptom: with the capacity controller installed, a briefed 5/28/33 came back from `run_mode.py pause` and `resume` as 1/1/2, while the resume message announced "caps primary 5, second 28, max-codex 33". Each tool's own tests passed: `test_run_mode.py` runs against a stub repository root with no controller, and `test_capacity_state_roundtrip.py` exercises the controller alone. Diagnosis: `apply` wrote the cap files itself and never seeded the controller, so `pause` asked a controller with no state to save the caps, it saved zeros, and `resume` restored its floor of 1 per account; the resume message was built from what the command intended to write rather than from what it read back, so the wrong numbers were announced confidently - which is precisely the 2026-09-12 resume script's failure, rebuilt. Fix: `apply` now calls `capacity_controller.py init` (a failure is a loud warning, since the caps it wrote are still correct), `resume` refuses when a cap file disagrees with the cap it restored, and its message reports the files rather than the intent; `scripts/tests/test_run_mode_capacity_roundtrip.py` pins the round trip against a repository root that has the controller in it. Lesson: when two tools each own part of one record, the test that matters is the one that installs both - and a report built from intent instead of from observation is a lie waiting for a deadline.

usage: gh_common.py pr-view [-h] number

positional arguments:
  number

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Usage: local/bin/janitor.sh [--dry-run] [--pass NAME]... [--list-passes]
#                             [--no-lock] [--report PATH] [--help]
#
# The self-repair pass.  ONE idempotent sweep, safe to run from cron or from the
# merge daemon's loop, that turns every terminal state the pipeline can reach
# into either a repair or a reported line.  Everything it does is selected by a
# record field — a session status, a marker's reason string, a PR state, a spool
# deadline — and never by a date glob or a filename digit filter.  The
# 2026-09-12 recovery script globbed `*20260912*.jsonl` and matched
# `/[0-9]{3}\.needs-attention$` with `-mmin -15`, so lanes below 100 and the 1xxx
# lanes were never repaired and a marker missed by one poll was never picked up
# again.  Nothing here has an age filter or a digit-count filter.
#
# The five passes, each independently guarded (one failing pass never aborts the
# others; a GitHub error is reported and retried next pass, never converted into
# a local success):
#
#   dead-sessions   results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl rows whose last status is
#                   `active` and whose process is gone.  When the capture ends in
#                   an exhausted reconnect, a 5xx or a concurrency refusal the
#                   same role is re-dispatched on the same PR and the same head,
#                   at most twice per (pr, role, head_sha), ledger
#                   $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/janitor/retries.jsonl.  A capture that
#                   ends cleanly is NEVER re-dispatched.  The abandoned row is
#                   marked `failed` so telemetry stops showing it live.
#                   This is the recovery path for the 25 reviews that were re-run
#                   by hand after the 503 outage: review.sh retries only a
#                   pre-model death (ended-started < 15 s and tokens 0), so a
#                   reviewer that dies after twenty minutes at
#                   "Reconnecting... 5/5" leaves the PR pending forever.
#                   SCOPE: only a role with a re-dispatch entry point is
#                   re-dispatched, and today that is `reviewer` alone
#                   (review.sh, exact head, verdict supersedes).  A dead prover,
#                   orc or fixer is marked `failed` with a `residue` field in
#                   $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/janitor/actions.jsonl and is the owning
#                   session's to re-plan; `local/bin/ready_report.py` counts
#                   those rows PER ROLE into the hourly comment on the progress
#                   issue, so the unrepaired remainder reaches the owner's
#                   channel instead of a local log.
#   parked-lanes    every $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/lanes/*.needs-attention, no digit
#                   filter and no age filter.  The recorded reason is classified;
#                   `merge` and `build` go to fix-lane.sh with the committed
#                   brief, at most twice per lane; every other class stays parked
#                   and appears in the report.
#   superseded-prs  local/bin/pr_janitor.py (empty three-dot diff AND head
#                   reachable from github/main; one idempotent marker comment;
#                   never closes an issue).
#   stale-lanes     lane state for lanes whose PR is closed or merged is deleted
#                   (20 stale 1xxx lanes were left behind on 2026-09-12).
#   spool-expiry    $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/capacity/spool/*.json entries past the
#                   run's dispatch_cutoff are dropped, so a spool that outlives a
#                   run cannot re-launch stale work.
#
# The janitor repairs; it never merges, never pushes, never closes an issue and
# never touches a gate.  Repairs are dispatched through fix-lane.sh ->
# dispatch.sh (agents never invoke codex directly) and the lane tail is
# relaunched through the repository's own local/bin/lane.sh.
#
# Runner: results/telemetry/owner-tools/merge-daemon.sh calls this once every
# `janitor_interval_s` (daemon.conf), detached and bounded; the sweep takes its
# own lock, so an overlapping call exits instead of doubling up.  Nothing else
# runs it: a checkout whose merge daemon is not running has no self-repair.
#
# Output: one line per action on stdout, the same lines in
# $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/janitor/report.md (the operator's log of the sweep; the
# hourly readiness report does NOT read it — it reports merges and readiness
# from daemon state) and one append-only JSONL row per action in
# $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/janitor/{retries,repairs,actions,closures}.jsonl.
#
# Exit codes: 0 all passes completed; 1 at least one pass failed (the others
# still ran); 2 usage/environment error.
#
# Environment:
#   MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT             override ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev
#   MIPSTARRE_REPO_ROOT              override the checkout (default: this file's)
#   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_RETRY_CAP      re-dispatches per (pr, role, head)  [2]
#   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_REPAIR_CAP     repairs per lane                    [2]
#   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_STALE_S        a dead session's capture must be this old
#                                    before it is judged abandoned       [900]
#   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_LANE_KEEP_S    lane state younger than this is never
#                                    deleted                             [3600]
#   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_REDISPATCH_ROLES  roles the janitor may re-dispatch
#                                    automatically; only a role with an entry
#                                    point below may be listed    [reviewer]
#   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_CLASSIFIER     auto | builtin  (auto prefers telemetry.py's
#                                    classify-failure when it exists)    [auto]
#   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_SOURCE_ONLY=1  define the functions and return; run nothing
#                                    (used by scripts/tests/test_janitor_classify.py)

set -uo pipefail

PROG="janitor.sh"

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="${MIPSTARRE_REPO_ROOT:-$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)}"
CACHE_ROOT="${MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT:-$HOME/.cache/mipstarre-dev}"
W="$CACHE_ROOT/watchdog"
L="$W/lanes"
D="$W/daemon"
J="$W/janitor"
SPOOL="$W/capacity/spool"
SESSIONS="${MIPSTARRE_SESSIONS_JSONL:-$REPO_ROOT/results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl}"

RETRY_CAP="${MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_RETRY_CAP:-2}"
REPAIR_CAP="${MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_REPAIR_CAP:-2}"
STALE_S="${MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_STALE_S:-900}"
LANE_KEEP_S="${MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_LANE_KEEP_S:-3600}"
REDISPATCH_ROLES="${MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_REDISPATCH_ROLES:-reviewer}"
CLASSIFIER="${MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_CLASSIFIER:-auto}"
BASE_REF="${MIPSTARRE_BASE_REF:-github/main}"

DRY_RUN=0
USE_LOCK=1
REPORT_FILE=""
PASS_FAILURES=0

ALL_PASSES="dead-sessions parked-lanes superseded-prs stale-lanes spool-expiry"
SELECTED="$ALL_PASSES"

# Report lines are collected in a file, not a variable: each pass runs in its own
# subshell so that one failing pass cannot abort the others, and a variable would
# not survive that boundary.
REPORT_SPOOL="${MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_REPORT_SPOOL:-$J/.report-lines.$$}"

# --------------------------------------------------------------- small helpers

now() { date -u +%FT%TZ; }

log() { printf '== %s %s\n' "$(now)" "$*"; }

# A reported line: printed, kept for report.md, and never silent.
report() {
  printf '%s\n' "$*"
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$REPORT_SPOOL")" 2>/dev/null || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$*" >> "$REPORT_SPOOL" 2>/dev/null || true
}

json_row() {
  python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps(dict(zip(sys.argv[1::2], sys.argv[2::2])), ensure_ascii=False))' "$@"
}

# Append-only JSONL under the cache root.  One short line per append, written
# with a single write(2), which is atomic for a line this size; the janitor also
# holds its own lock, so two passes never interleave.
ledger_append() {
  local file="$1"; shift
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$file")" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "$(json_row "$@")" >> "$file"
}

# Count attempt rows in a ledger for one key.  Field-based, never a date glob.
ledger_count() {
  JAN_LEDGER="$1" JAN_KEY="$2" python3 - <<'PY'
import json, os
path, key, total = os.environ["JAN_LEDGER"], os.environ["JAN_KEY"], 0
try:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as handle:
        for line in handle:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            try:
                row = json.loads(line)
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if isinstance(row, dict) and row.get("key") == key and row.get("event") == "attempt":
                total += 1
except FileNotFoundError:
    pass
print(total)
PY
}

retry_key() { printf 'pr%s:%s:%s\n' "$1" "$2" "$3"; }

# Exit 0 while another attempt is allowed.  The cap is on attempts, not on
# successes: a re-dispatch that dies again counts.
retry_allow() {
  return 1
}

cutoff_passed() {
  [ -n "$DISPATCH_CUTOFF_EPOCH" ] || return 1
  [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$DISPATCH_CUTOFF_EPOCH" ]
}

resolve_cutoff() {
  local raw="$DISPATCH_CUTOFF_RAW"
  [ -n "$raw" ] || raw="$(run_mode_field dispatch_cutoff)"
  case "$(printf '%s' "$raw" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" in
    ''|'until my word'|none|never|unlimited) DISPATCH_CUTOFF_EPOCH=""; return 0 ;;
  esac
  DISPATCH_CUTOFF_EPOCH="$(python3 - "$raw" <<'PY' 2>/dev/null || true
import sys
from datetime import datetime

text = sys.argv[1].strip()
if text.endswith("Z"):
    text = text[:-1] + "+00:00"
try:
    parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(text)
except ValueError:
    raise SystemExit(0)
if parsed.tzinfo is None:
    raise SystemExit(0)
print(int(parsed.timestamp()))
PY
)"
  [ -n "$DISPATCH_CUTOFF_EPOCH" ] || die 4 "cannot read the dispatch cutoff '$raw'.
  It must be ISO-8601 with an offset (2026-09-13T08:00:00Z) or the literal
  \"until my word\". Fix run.dispatch_cutoff in $RUN_MODE_JSON, or unset
  MIPSTARRE_DISPATCH_CUTOFF."
}

write_spool() {
  # The whole request, before the first reservation, so a dispatch the provider
  # refused can be replayed by the janitor instead of being lost.
  local state="$1"
  [ -n "$SPOOL_FILE" ] || return 0
  mkdir -p "$SPOOL_DIR"
  python3 - "$SPOOL_FILE" "$state" "$NAME_BASE" "$NAME" "$ROLE" "$ISSUE" "$PR_ID" \
    "$WORKTREE_ABS" "$BRANCH" "$PERSONA_LABEL" "$PERSONA_REF" "$EFFORT" "$JOB_CLASS" \
    "$HARDNESS_REASON" "$SPOOL_PROMPT" "$SANDBOX" "$ACCOUNT_REQUESTED" "$ATTEMPT" \
    "$MAX_ATTEMPTS" "$DISPATCH_CUTOFF_EPOCH" "$DISPATCHER" "$RESUME_ID" \
    "$CONTINUATION_FILE" "$KEY_LABEL" "$ENDPOINT_LABEL" "$FAILURE_CLASS" <<'PY'
import json, os, sys, tempfile, time

KEYS = ("state", "base_name", "name", "role", "issue", "pr", "worktree", "branch",
        "persona", "persona_ref", "effort", "job_class", "hardness_reason",
        "prompt_file", "sandbox", "account", "attempt", "max_attempts",
        "deadline_epoch", "dispatcher", "resume", "continue_from", "key_label",
        "endpoint", "failure_class")
path, values = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2:]
if len(values) != len(KEYS):
    sys.stderr.write("dispatch.sh: spool argument count mismatch\n")
    raise SystemExit(2)
record = {key: (value if value != "" else None) for key, value in zip(KEYS, values)}
record["attempt"] = int(record["attempt"] or 1)
record["max_attempts"] = int(record["max_attempts"] or 1)
record["deadline_epoch"] = int(record["deadline_epoch"]) if record["deadline_epoch"] else None
record["spooled_at"] = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z")
record["pid"] = os.getppid()
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
handle = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", encoding="utf-8",
                                     dir=os.path.dirname(path), delete=False)
try:
    json.dump(record, handle, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
    handle.write("\n")
    handle.flush()
    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
finally:
    handle.close()
os.replace(handle.name, path)
PY
}

clear_spool() {
  [ -n "$SPOOL_FILE" ] || return 0
  rm -f "$SPOOL_FILE" "$SPOOL_PROMPT"
}

transient_class() {
  case "$1" in
    refused|endpoint_down|concurrency_limit|endpoint_5xx|retries_exhausted) return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}

retry_is_safe() {
  # A transient CLASS is not by itself a licence to re-run the prompt.
  # `refused`, `endpoint_down`, `concurrency_limit` and `endpoint_5xx` are
  # admission failures: the model never ran, the worktree was never touched, and
  # a retry is a pure re-attempt.  `retries_exhausted` is different — the client
  # gave up reconnecting, which can happen twenty minutes in, and re-running the
  # same prompt from scratch in a worktree that now holds the dead session's
  # partial, uncommitted edits is not a retry, it is a second worker on a dirty
  # tree.  review.sh already draws this line (ended-started < 15 s, tokens 0);
  # draw the same one here: retry only a death that did no work and left a clean
  # tree.  Anything else is left to the janitor's dead-session pass, which
  # re-dispatches under a per-(pr, role, head) budget with the state in hand.
  local dirty=""
  if [ "${WORKTREE_STATUS_AFTER_CODEX:-}" != "${WORKTREE_STATUS_BEFORE_CODEX:-}" ]; then
    dirty="${WORKTREE_STATUS_AFTER_CODEX:-}"
  fi
  [ "${DISPATCH_STATUS:-}" = refused ] || return 1
  [ "${DISPATCH_TURNS:-0}" = 0 ] || return 1
  case "${DISPATCH_USAGE_TOTAL:-0}" in
    ''|0) ;;
    *) note "not retrying '$FAILURE_CLASS': the session used ${DISPATCH_USAGE_TOTAL} tokens \
before dying, so a re-run would repeat work in a tree that holds its partial edits"
       return 1 ;;
  esac
  if [ -n "$dirty" ]; then
    note "not retrying '$FAILURE_CLASS': $WORKTREE_ABS has uncommitted changes from the \
dead session; the janitor's dead-session pass owns this one"
    return 1
  fi
  return 0
}

backoff_or_give_up() {
  # Jittered exponential backoff, base 30 s and cap 10 min. Returns 0 to retry.
  local exponent delay jitter total
  if [ "$ATTEMPT" -ge "$MAX_ATTEMPTS" ]; then
    note "attempt $ATTEMPT of $MAX_ATTEMPTS ended '$FAILURE_CLASS'; no attempt left"
    return 1
  fi
  if cutoff_passed; then
    note "the run's dispatch cutoff has passed; not retrying after '$FAILURE_CLASS'"
    return 1
  fi
  exponent=$((ATTEMPT - 1))
  [ "$exponent" -le 20 ] || exponent=20
  delay=$((BACKOFF_BASE_S * (1 << exponent)))
  [ "$delay" -le "$BACKOFF_MAX_S" ] || delay="$BACKOFF_MAX_S"
  jitter=$((RANDOM % (delay / 2 + 1)))
  total=$((delay + jitter))
  ATTEMPT=$((ATTEMPT + 1))
  write_spool retrying
  note "attempt $((ATTEMPT - 1)) of $MAX_ATTEMPTS ended '$FAILURE_CLASS'; \
retrying as attempt $ATTEMPT in ${total}s"
  sleep "$total"
  if cutoff_passed; then
    note "the run's dispatch cutoff passed during the backoff; stopping"
    return 1
  fi
  return 0
}

report_and_exit_refused() {
  # One `refused` row for the whole episode, then exit 7 with the spool intact.
  # `refused` is not `failed`: the dispatch was never admitted, so it must not
  # be scored as a failed attempt against a proof packet's budget.
  local ts
  ts="$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z)"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 0 ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "{\"type\":\"dispatch.refused\",\"failure_class\":\"$FAILURE_CLASS\",\
\"attempts\":$ATTEMPT,\"account\":\"$ACCOUNT_REQUESTED\",\"endpoint\":\"$ENDPOINT_LABEL\",\
\"ts\":\"$ts\"}" >"$CAPTURE"
    cp "$CAPTURE" "$PUBLISHED_CAPTURE_DIR/$NAME.jsonl" 2>/dev/null ||
      note "warning: could not copy the refusal record into $PUBLISHED_CAPTURE_DIR"
    REFUSED_ARGS=(--repo-root "$REPO_ROOT" session-summarize
      "$PUBLISHED_CAPTURE_DIR/$NAME.jsonl" --name "$NAME" --role "$ROLE" --issue "$ISSUE"
      --start "$START_TS" --end "$ts" --dispatcher "$DISPATCHER" --worktree "$WORKTREE_ABS"
      --status refused --failure-class "$FAILURE_CLASS" --key-label "$KEY_LABEL"
      --endpoint "$ENDPOINT_LABEL" --no-rollout-scan --append-to "$REGISTRY")
    [ -z "$PR_ID" ] || REFUSED_ARGS+=(--pr "$PR_ID")
    python3 "$TELEMETRY_PY" "${REFUSED_ARGS[@]}" >/dev/null ||
      note "warning: could not record the refusal for $NAME; the capture is at $CAPTURE"
  fi
  printf 'name: %s\n' "$NAME"
  printf 'account: %s\n' "$ACCOUNT_REQUESTED"
  printf 'endpoint: %s\n' "$ENDPOINT_LABEL"
  printf 'failure_class: %s\n' "$FAILURE_CLASS"
  printf 'attempts: %s\n' "$ATTEMPT"
  printf 'spool: %s\n' "${SPOOL_FILE:-none}"

This is the **single\nsource of truth** for agent conventions. Claude Code agents should also read\n`CLAUDE.md` for Claude-specific notes.\n\n## Project Overview\n\nThis repository is a Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization project for mathematics\naround $MIP^* = RE$. It is the **local-only continuation** of\n[LionSR/MIPStarRE](https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE): the inherited track is\nthe **low individual degree test (LDT)** paper (arXiv:2009.12982); the active\ntrack is the **quantum Pauli basis test (QPBT)** from *MIP\\*=RE*\n(arXiv:2001.04383, primary) and *NEEXP in MIP\\** (arXiv:1904.05870, secondary).\n\nCI, review, and auto-fix **execute locally**; issues, PRs, their evidence and\nmerges live on GitHub (`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`), reached only through\n`local/bin/gh_common.py`. Read `local/README.md` and `local/DESIGN.md` before\ndoing workflow actions; the `## Local Operations` section below summarizes the\nrules.\n\nKey locations:\n\n- `references/qpbt-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of MIP\\*=RE\n  (arXiv:2001.04383); the QPBT lives in\n  `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex` and\n  `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex`\n- `references/neexp-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of NEEXP in MIP\\*\n  (arXiv:1904.05870); secondary source\n  (`07_a_self_test_for_the_pauli_basis.tex`)\n- `references/ldt-paper/` — in-repo TeX source mirror for LDT\n- `blueprint/src/` — active LaTeX blueprint with Lean cross-references\n  (`\\lean{}`, `\\leanok`)\n- `MIPStarRE/` — Lean codebase matching the blueprint\n- `audits/` — dated audit reports, scouting notes, and repair plans\n- `local/`, `results/telemetry/` — the local workflow layer\n\nA legacy 2111 tensor track exists under `blueprint/legacy/` — do not modify it.\n\n**Canonical source hierarchy** (use in this order):\n\n1. `references/` paper mirrors — TeX source of the papers\n2. `blueprint/src/chapter/` — active LaTeX blueprint\n3. `MIPStarRE/` — Lean scaffold\n\nAlways read the paper source before formalizing or proving a statement. The\npaper contains the precise mathematical definitions, theorem statements, and\nproof strategies that the Lean code must faithfully represent. When stuck on a\nsorry site or proof, go back to the original paper TeX source — the answer is\nalmost always there. Do not guess or try random tactics without first\nunderstanding the paper's proof strategy.\n\n## Repository Layout\n\n```\nMIPStarRE/\n├── Quantum/               # Reusable matrix / measurement infrastructure\n│   ├── FiniteMatrix.lean  # Op d, normalizedTrace, tauNormSq, IsProj, ...\n│   └── Measurement.lean   # POVM, measurement types\n└── LDT/                   # Low individual degree test (13 submodules)\n    ├── Basic/             # Parameters, operators, distributions, submeasurements\n    ├── Test/              # Test definitions & main theorem\n    ├── Preliminaries/\n    ├── MakingMeasurementsProjective/\n    ├── MainInductionStep/\n    ├── ExpansionHypercubeGraph/\n    ├── GlobalVariance/\n    ├── SelfImprovement/\n    ├── CommutativityPoints/\n    ├── Commutativity/\n    └── Pasting/\n```\n\nEach LDT submodule typically has `Defs.lean` and `Theorems.lean`. Root imports\nflow: `MIPStarRE.lean` → `Quantum` + `LDT` → all submodules.\n\n## Quick Start — Build and Check Commands\n\nRun commands from the repository root unless noted otherwise.\n\n### First-time setup\n\n```bash\nlake exe cache get\nlake build\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check\n```\n\nRun the hook check in every fresh worktree before preparing a PR.  The hooks\nmove fast statement-integrity, proof-debt, changed-file Lean, and blueprint-sync\nchecks to the local workflow so CI is not spent on preventable statement drift.\n\n### Full project build (CI-equivalent)\n\n```bash\nlake build\n```\n\n### Fast single-file type-check (default iteration loop)\n\n```bash\nlake env lean MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in one file\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean || true\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in the whole project\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE\n```\n\n### Declaration checker\n\n```bash\nlake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls\n```\n\nUse this when blueprint declaration lists need to match Lean declarations.\n\n### Blueprint build\n\n```bash\nleanblueprint pdf    # PDF output\nleanblueprint web    # HTML output (use as default for quick checks)\n```\n\nIn CI, blueprint linting effectively runs `leanblueprint web` from `blueprint/`.\n\n### What counts as a single test\n\nThis repository does not have a conventional unit-test suite. The closest\nsingle-test commands are:\n\n- **Lean work**: `lake env lean path/to/File.lean` and\n  `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\" path/to/File.lean || true`\n- **Blueprint work**: `leanblueprint web`\n- **Whole-repo verification**: `lake build` and\n  `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\n\n### Recommended validation sequence\n\nFor a Lean file change:\n\n1. Type-check the edited file with `lake env lean ...`\n2. Scan that file for `sorry|axiom`\n3. If the change affects imports or shared declarations, run `lake build`\n\nFor blueprint changes:\n\n1. Run `leanblueprint web`\n2. If declaration links changed, run `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\n\n## Toolchain\n\n- **Lean**: v4.31.0 (from `lean-toolchain`)\n- **Mathlib**: v4.31.0 (from `lakefile.toml`)\n\nImportant `lakefile.toml` options:\n\n- `relaxedAutoImplicit = false` — declare all variables explicitly\n- `pp.unicode.fun = true`\n- `weak.linter.mathlibStandardSet = true`\n- `maxSynthPendingDepth = 3`\n\n## Proof-Filling Order\n\nSections must be filled in this dependency order:\n\n1. Sections 3–4: test setup and preliminaries\n2. Section 5: making measurements projective\n3. Sections 7–8: expansion and global variance\n4. Section 9: self-improvement\n5. Sections 10–11: commutativity\n6. Section 12: pasting\n7. Section 6: main induction wrapper\n\nDo not start from the final theorem and guess intermediate facts.\n\n## Faithful Formalization Policy\n\nA declaration is a formalization of a paper theorem only when its public Lean\nstatement matches the cited paper statement, up to faithful formal encoding.\nChanging a Lean theorem away from the corresponding statement in\n`references/ldt-paper/` is strongly discouraged and should occur only when a\nfaithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical necessity requires it.\nThis applies to every declaration advertised as a formalization of a paper\nresult, not only to theorems currently undergoing repair.  The check is on the\nhypotheses as well as the conclusion.  A theorem whose\nconclusion has the right shape but whose assumptions include an extra\nload-bearing bridge input or hypotheses bundle is a conditional theorem, not\nthe paper theorem.\nThe project goal is to eliminate such conditional bridges, not to normalize\nthem as permanent infrastructure.\n\nIf the only available Lean theorem has extra assumptions, the blueprint must\nnot mark the source-labelled paper entry as matched by that theorem.  Either\nleave the source-labelled entry without `\\leanok`, or state the restricted or\nconditional result as a separate Lean-only blueprint entry whose hypotheses are\ndisplayed explicitly.  A scope-restricted theorem may be marked `\\leanok` only\nagainst a blueprint statement that explicitly states the restriction; it must\nnot be presented as the unrestricted source theorem.\n\nWhen a stricter-hypothesis Lean theorem is the only available version near a\nsource theorem, the discrepancy must have a paper-gap note or tracking issue.\nThe note should identify the missing hypothesis, explain why it is not part of\nthe cited statement, and state the plan for eliminating the restriction,\nderiving it internally, or moving the result out of the source-labelled route.\n\nThis rule applies especially to declarations named after paper labels such as\n`mainFormal`, `selfImprovement`, `mainInduction`, or other theorem names linked\nfrom the blueprint by `\\lean{...}` and `\\leanok`.\n\nBefore editing any theorem tagged with a paper label (`thm:*`, `lem:*`,\n`prop:*`):\n\n1. Read the corresponding statement in `references/ldt-paper/`.\n2. Preserve the public Lean theorem statement, except for hypotheses that are\n   genuinely part of the faithful encoding of the paper's domain.\n3. Do not add bridge inputs, residual packages, repair hypotheses, producer\n   assumptions, generic hypotheses or assumptions bundles, or arbitrary\n   implication hypotheses to the paper theorem.\n4. If a missing intermediate fact is needed, first state that fact as a named\n   lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.\n5. Do not add a conditional helper merely to keep a file compiling.  A\n   conditional helper may remain temporarily only when the proof content it\n   preserves is mathematically useful, the source-faithful theorem remains\n   visible, and the helper has a paper-gap note, a named construction theorem\n   or proof-obligation target, and an explicit discharge or deletion plan.  Its\n   name must show that it is conditional without making the assumption look like\n   an acceptable source hypothesis, for example\n   `mainFormal_ofInternalObligations`, `selfImprovementFromObligations`, or a\n   name ending in `_ofObligations`.\n6. Do not point a source-labelled blueprint theorem to the conditional helper\n   with `\\leanok`.\n\nWhen reviewing an existing bridge, residual, repair, producer, or package\nhypothesis, first try to recover any genuine proof content from its construction\nand turn that content into a source-faithful lemma.  If the bridge does not\nactually follow from the paper hypotheses, do not preserve the paper theorem as\na strengthened statement.  Restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave\nthe missing proof obligation explicit, even if that means reintroducing a\ntracked `sorry` during a repair PR.\n\nSome side conditions are not deviations: positivity needed to define a\ndivision, nonemptiness of a finite type, decidability instances, field-model\ninstances, and similar boundary hypotheses may be faithful encodings of\nassumptions that the paper leaves implicit.  These should still be reviewed and\ndocumented if they are mathematically load-bearing.  The forbidden pattern is\ndifferent: moving an unproved step of the proof into the theorem statement, such\nas a `BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`,\n`Producer`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic `Assumptions` assumption that the\npaper theorem does not assume.  These assumptions\nshould not be introduced merely to keep a file compiling or to avoid a `sorry`;\nthey require explicit mathematical justification and a planned discharge.\n\nFor the current LDT final theorem, `mainFormal` is reserved for the statement of\n`\\Cref{thm:main-formal}`: from a projective strategy passing the low individual\ndegree test, it produces the three final consistency conclusions.  A theorem\nwith an extra hypothesis such as\n`hbaseBridge : ... → MainFormalRepairedBridgeHypotheses ...` is temporary\nscaffolding at best; it must not be the declaration advertised as\n`thm:main-formal`.  The corresponding paper-aligned version should remain\nvisible, even if its proof is temporarily unfinished during repair.\n\nEvery agent changing a paper-labelled theorem must finish with a statement\nintegrity audit:\n\n- paper assumptions;\n- Lean assumptions;\n- paper conclusion;\n- Lean conclusion;\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\n\n### Paper-realignment mode\n\nWhen a theorem, definition, or hypothesis field has already drifted away from\n`references/ldt-paper/`, a repair PR may temporarily reintroduce `sorry` in\norder to restore the source-faithful statement.  In this mode, statement\nfaithfulness is the first invariant: keeping a divergent proof intact merely to\navoid `sorry` preserves a theorem that the paper does not state.\n\nPaper-realignment mode is narrow.  It applies only to edits whose purpose is to\nremove wrong hypotheses, delete divergent fields, restore a paper theorem\nstatement, or replace a conditional theorem by a paper-facing statement plus a\nnamed proof obligation.  Such a PR must:\n\n1. cite the paper passage by label or line range in the relevant docstring;\n2. cite the paper-gap note or tracking issue that records the divergence;\n3. identify every introduced or retained `sorry` and the construction theorem,\n   proof-obligation theorem, or source-faithful lemma expected to discharge it;\n4. avoid unrelated refactors, notation changes, or proof-engineering churn.\n\nDuring paper realignment, every restated definition, hypothesis field, or\npaper-facing theorem must have a docstring that lets a reviewer tell whether\nthe statement is present in the paper or is a Lean-only proof obligation.  A\nname such as `Bridge`, `Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Input`, or `Producer`\nis not by itself a mathematical source citation.\n\n### Unfaithful dependency markers\n\nA theorem or lemma is **unfaithful** when its proof relies on a hypothesis,\nhelper, bridge, residual, repair input, or conditional theorem that is known not\nto follow from the cited paper statement.  This includes the case where the\npublic theorem statement is source-shaped but the proof calls a conditional\nhelper whose load-bearing hypothesis is not yet derived from the paper\nhypotheses.\n\nSuch a declaration must carry a docstring section beginning with\n`**Unfaithful:**`.  The marker must name the load-bearing deviation, cite the\npaper-gap note or issue that documents it, and state the planned discharge.  A\nminimal form is:\n\n```text\n**Unfaithful:** This proof currently relies on `<hypothesis or helper>`,\nwhich is not derived from `<paper label or line range>`.  Documented in\n`docs/paper-gaps/<note>.tex` or issue `#N`.  Elimination: prove\n`<construction theorem>` from the paper hypotheses.\n```\n\nThe marker propagates through dependencies: a theorem whose proof transitively\nuses an unfaithful declaration is itself unfaithful until the dependency is\nreplaced by a source-faithful proof.  Remove the marker only when the cited\ndeviation has been discharged.\n\nNot every discrepancy requires the full `**Unfaithful:**` marker.  If the paper\nhas a local typo, a documented numerical strengthening, or a genuine scope\nrestriction, use a lighter docstring marker such as `**Local fix:**` or\n`**Scope restriction:**`, citing the relevant paper-gap note.  These lighter\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\npaper hypotheses.\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Imports\n\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\n- One import per line\n- Follow existing local import style\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\n\n### File structure\n\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\n\n1. imports\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\n3. namespace / opens / variables\n4. declarations\n\n### Formatting\n\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\n  own line\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\n  theorem statement\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\n  tactic blocks.\n\n### Naming conventions\n\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\n\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\n\nProject-preferred variable names:\n\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\n- `σ` — strategies\n- `P` — projective measurements\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\n\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\n\n### Types and signatures\n\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\n  wrappers\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\n\n### Documentation\n\nRequired:\n\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\n\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\lean{...}`\nand `\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\n\n## Proof Engineering\n\n### Search before proving\n\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\n\n### Mathlib integration\n\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. When proving lemmas:\n\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\n\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\n\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\n\n### Validation ladder\n\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\n2. `lake build`\n\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\n\n### Lean-specific advice\n\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\n  already in the repo\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\n\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\n\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. Prefer a\nclear, precise, and unhurried expository style: introduce the object under\ndiscussion, state the mathematical relation being used, distinguish hypotheses\nfrom conclusions, and avoid informal process language when a standard\nmathematical phrase is available.\n\nWhen writing docstrings, audit notes, PR descriptions, or blueprint-adjacent\ncomments, use terminology from the standard mathematical literature, the LDT\npaper, and the local formalization. Do not invent slang or private shorthand for\nmathematical objects. The goal is prose that a third-party reader can understand\nwithout having read the agent conversation that produced the change.\n\n### Paper-gap notes\n\nFor the proof-gap terminology used to distinguish source theorems, internal\nproof obligations, and conditional helpers, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.  For documentation of discrepancies\nbetween the cited paper, the blueprint, and Lean, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex`. In particular, such notes should be\nmathematical prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists who have not\nread the issue discussion: introduce notation, state the cited assertion,\nisolate the calculation or logical obstruction, compare with the blueprint and\nLean statement, and give a clear verdict. If Lean uses a Mathlib result or\nconstruction not present in the cited argument, explain that replacement\npedagogically before naming the formal declaration. If the cited assertion is\nfalse and a counterexample is available, explain the counterexample in prose and\nuse any Lean declaration only as verification.\n\n## Proof Integrity\n\n### Blockers (must be resolved before merge)\n\nSee the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md` for the full catalog.\n\n**Direct proof holes**: `sorry`, `admit`\n\n**Kernel / type system bypasses**: `native_decide`, `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce`,\n`lcProof`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`\n\n**Axiom smuggling**: unjustified `axiom` declarations\n\n**Circular reasoning**: proofs that assume the statement being proved as a local\nhypothesis, or helper lemmas that essentially restate the main goal.\n\n**Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)**: custom re-declarations of standard\nMathlib lemmas; `axiom` or `sorry`-based helpers for facts already in Mathlib;\nchains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core.\n\n**Scaffolding that blocks real formalization**: definitions or theorem statements\nthat do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics, making them impossible\nto connect to real Mathlib-based proofs. Ask: *Can a real proof be built on top\nof this?*\n\n### Warnings\n\nPlaceholder tactics (`exact?`, `apply?`, `library_search`) should be replaced\nwith concrete results. Debug artifacts (`dbg_trace`, `#check`, `#eval`,\n`#print`) should be removed from proof files. See the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference for\nthe full warning catalog.\n\n### Anti-patterns\n\nSubtler proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks yet still fail to\nprove the claimed mathematics are catalogued in `docs/anti_patterns.md`:\nconclusion-shaped hypotheses, definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback\nbranches, trivial default witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, and external\n`*Statement` smuggles. Reviewers should consult this file alongside\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md`.\n\n## PR and Commit Conventions\n\nPRs are GitHub pull requests (opened by `local/bin/pr_open.py`, merged by\n`local/bin/pr_merge.py`); `#N` in PR bodies and commit messages is the GitHub\nissue number. Titles, bodies, and commit rules below are unchanged from the\nparent project.\n\n### PR title format\n\n```\ntype(scope): short description\n```\n\n| Type       | When to use                                      |\n|------------|--------------------------------------------------|\n| `feat`     | New definition, lemma, theorem, or module         |\n| `fix`      | Bug fix (broken proof, wrong identifier, etc.)    |\n| `refactor` | Restructuring without changing API surface        |\n| `docs`     | Documentation or blueprint changes only           |\n| `style`    | Formatting, naming, or docstring cleanup only     |\n| `ci`       | CI/CD workflow changes                            |\n| `chore`    | Dependency bumps, linting, toolchain updates      |\n\n**Scope** is a shortened module path: `LDT/SelfImprovement`, `Quantum`,\n`blueprint`, etc. Omit the `MIPStarRE/` prefix.\n\n### PR body template\n\nEvery PR body must contain three sections:\n\n```markdown\n### Motivation\n- Why this change is needed. Cite the issue and paper/blueprint location.\n\n### Description\n- State precisely what changed.\n\n### Testing\n- What was verified and how (e.g., `lake build`, `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\"`).\n\n---\nAddresses #N\n```\n\nUse `Addresses #N` (keeps the issue open) or `Closes #N` (auto-closes on merge).\n\n### Commit messages\n\n- **Imperative mood** in the subject line (\"Add\", not \"Added\")\n- Subject under 72 characters\n- When squash-merging, the commit message should match the PR title format\n\n## Review Process\n\nEvery PR touching Lean code is reviewed by a dedicated local reviewer session\n(`local/bin/review.sh`, dispatched after green local CI; a session never\nreviews its own diff) against these criteria:\n\n1. **Proof correctness** — No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.\n2. **Mathlib style** — Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_doc` references.\n3. **Paper terminology** — Public Lean names and documentation should use\n   terminology from the paper and blueprint. See `docs/mathematical_language.md`.\n4. **Linter hygiene** — Fix warnings, don't mask them with broad\n   `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks.\n5. **Type safety** — No universe mismatches, coercion problems.\n6. **Performance** — Avoid expensive tactics on large types.\n7. **Modularity** — Are new lemmas general enough to be reused?\n8. **Documentation** — Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.\n9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** — Add `\\lean{}` and `\\leanok` tags for\n   formalized statements only when the Lean statement matches the source.\n   Record formalization-only auxiliary lemmas explicitly.\n10. **Scaffolding integrity** — Verify scaffolding aligns with Mathlib.\n11. **Statement drift** — Compare source-labelled theorem statements with the\n   paper and flag new hypotheses, weakened conclusions, changed quantifier\n   order, altered error parameters, or bridge/residual packages moving toward\n   a paper theorem.\n12. **Proof-evasion anti-patterns** — Review against `docs/anti_patterns.md`.\n\nFor full details, see `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` and the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review` reference.\n\n## Blueprint and Documentation It applies only to edits whose purpose is to\nremove wrong hypotheses, delete divergent fields, restore a paper theorem\nstatement, or replace a conditional theorem by a paper-facing statement plus a\nnamed proof obligation.  Such a PR must:\n\n1. cite the paper passage by label or line range in the relevant docstring;\n2. cite the paper-gap note or tracking issue that records the divergence;\n3. identify every introduced or retained `sorry` and the construction theorem,\n   proof-obligation theorem, or source-faithful lemma expected to discharge it;\n4. avoid unrelated refactors, notation changes, or proof-engineering churn.\n\nDuring paper realignment, every restated definition, hypothesis field, or\npaper-facing theorem must have a docstring that lets a reviewer tell whether\nthe statement is present in the paper or is a Lean-only proof obligation.  A\nname such as `Bridge`, `Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Input`, or `Producer`\nis not by itself a mathematical source citation.\n\n### Unfaithful dependency markers\n\nA theorem or lemma is **unfaithful** when its proof relies on a hypothesis,\nhelper, bridge, residual, repair input, or conditional theorem that is known not\nto follow from the cited paper statement.  This includes the case where the\npublic theorem statement is source-shaped but the proof calls a conditional\nhelper whose load-bearing hypothesis is not yet derived from the paper\nhypotheses.\n\nSuch a declaration must carry a docstring section beginning with\n`**Unfaithful:**`.  The marker must name the load-bearing deviation, cite the\npaper-gap note or issue that documents it, and state the planned discharge.  A\nminimal form is:\n\n```text\n**Unfaithful:** This proof currently relies on `<hypothesis or helper>`,\nwhich is not derived from `<paper label or line range>`.  Documented in\n`docs/paper-gaps/<note>.tex` or issue `#N`.  Elimination: prove\n`<construction theorem>` from the paper hypotheses.\n```\n\nThe marker propagates through dependencies: a theorem whose proof transitively\nuses an unfaithful declaration is itself unfaithful until the dependency is\nreplaced by a source-faithful proof.  Remove the marker only when the cited\ndeviation has been discharged.\n\nNot every discrepancy requires the full `**Unfaithful:**` marker.  If the paper\nhas a local typo, a documented numerical strengthening, or a genuine scope\nrestriction, use a lighter docstring marker such as `**Local fix:**` or\n`**Scope restriction:**`, citing the relevant paper-gap note.  These lighter\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\npaper hypotheses.\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Imports\n\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\n- One import per line\n- Follow existing local import style\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\n\n### File structure\n\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\n\n1. imports\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\n3. namespace / opens / variables\n4. declarations\n\n### Formatting\n\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\n  own line\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\n  theorem statement\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\n  tactic blocks.\n\n### Naming conventions\n\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\n\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\n\nProject-preferred variable names:\n\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\n- `σ` — strategies\n- `P` — projective measurements\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\n\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\n\n### Types and signatures\n\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\n  wrappers\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\n\n### Documentation\n\nRequired:\n\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\n\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\lean{...}`\nand `\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\n\n## Proof Engineering\n\n### Search before proving\n\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\n\n### Mathlib integration\n\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. When proving lemmas:\n\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\n\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\n\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\n\n### Validation ladder\n\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\n2. `lake build`\n\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\n\n### Lean-specific advice\n\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\n  already in the repo\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\n\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\n\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. Prefer a\nclear, precise, and unhurried expository style: introduce the object under\ndiscussion, state the mathematical relation being used, distinguish hypotheses\nfrom conclusions, and avoid informal process language when a standard\nmathematical phrase is available.\n\nWhen writing docstrings, audit notes, PR descriptions, or blueprint-adjacent\ncomments, use terminology from the standard mathematical literature, the LDT\npaper, and the local formalization. Do not invent slang or private shorthand for\nmathematical objects. The goal is prose that a third-party reader can understand\nwithout having read the agent conversation that produced the change.\n\n### Paper-gap notes\n\nFor the proof-gap terminology used to distinguish source theorems, internal\nproof obligations, and conditional helpers, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.  For documentation of discrepancies\nbetween the cited paper, the blueprint, and Lean, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex`. In particular, such notes should be\nmathematical prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists who have not\nread the issue discussion: introduce notation, state the cited assertion,\nisolate the calculation or logical obstruction, compare with the blueprint and\nLean statement, and give a clear verdict. If Lean uses a Mathlib result or\nconstruction not present in the cited argument, explain that replacement\npedagogically before naming the formal declaration. If the cited assertion is\nfalse and a counterexample is available, explain the counterexample in prose and\nuse any Lean declaration only as verification.\n\n## Proof Integrity\n\n### Blockers (must be resolved before merge)\n\nSee the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md` for the full catalog.\n\n**Direct proof holes**: `sorry`, `admit`\n\n**Kernel / type system bypasses**: `native_decide`, `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce`,\n`lcProof`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`\n\n**Axiom smuggling**: unjustified `axiom` declarations\n\n**Circular reasoning**: proofs that assume the statement being proved as a local\nhypothesis, or helper lemmas that essentially restate the main goal.\n\n**Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)**: custom re-declarations of standard\nMathlib lemmas; `axiom` or `sorry`-based helpers for facts already in Mathlib;\nchains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core.\n\n**Scaffolding that blocks real formalization**: definitions or theorem statements\nthat do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics, making them impossible\nto connect to real Mathlib-based proofs. Ask: *Can a real proof be built on top\nof this?*\n\n### Warnings\n\nPlaceholder tactics (`exact?`, `apply?`, `library_search`) should be replaced\nwith concrete results. Debug artifacts (`dbg_trace`, `#check`, `#eval`,\n`#print`) should be removed from proof files. See the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference for\nthe full warning catalog.\n\n### Anti-patterns\n\nSubtler proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks yet still fail to\nprove the claimed mathematics are catalogued in `docs/anti_patterns.md`:\nconclusion-shaped hypotheses, definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback\nbranches, trivial default witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, and external\n`*Statement` smuggles. Reviewers should consult this file alongside\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md`.\n\n## PR and Commit Conventions\n\nPRs are GitHub pull requests (opened by `local/bin/pr_open.py`, merged by\n`local/bin/pr_merge.py`); `#N` in PR bodies and commit messages is the GitHub\nissue number. Titles, bodies, and commit rules below are unchanged from the\nparent project.\n\n### PR title format\n\n```\ntype(scope): short description\n```\n\n| Type       | When to use                                      |\n|------------|--------------------------------------------------|\n| `feat`     | New definition, lemma, theorem, or module         |\n| `fix`      | Bug fix (broken proof, wrong identifier, etc.)    |\n| `refactor` | Restructuring without changing API surface        |\n| `docs`     | Documentation or blueprint changes only           |\n| `style`    | Formatting, naming, or docstring cleanup only     |\n| `ci`       | CI/CD workflow changes                            |\n| `chore`    | Dependency bumps, linting, toolchain updates      |\n\n**Scope** is a shortened module path: `LDT/SelfImprovement`, `Quantum`,\n`blueprint`, etc. Omit the `MIPStarRE/` prefix.\n\n### PR body template\n\nEvery PR body must contain three sections:\n\n```markdown\n### Motivation\n- Why this change is needed. Cite the issue and paper/blueprint location.\n\n### Description\n- State precisely what changed.\n\n### Testing\n- What was verified and how (e.g., `lake build`, `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\"`).\n\n---\nAddresses #N\n```\n\nUse `Addresses #N` (keeps the issue open) or `Closes #N` (auto-closes on merge).\n\n### Commit messages\n\n- **Imperative mood** in the subject line (\"Add\", not \"Added\")\n- Subject under 72 characters\n- When squash-merging, the commit message should match the PR title format\n\n## Review Process\n\nEvery PR touching Lean code is reviewed by a dedicated local reviewer session\n(`local/bin/review.sh`, dispatched after green local CI; a session never\nreviews its own diff) against these criteria:\n\n1. **Proof correctness** — No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.\n2. **Mathlib style** — Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_doc` references.\n3. **Paper terminology** — Public Lean names and documentation should use\n   terminology from the paper and blueprint. See `docs/mathematical_language.md`.\n4. **Linter hygiene** — Fix warnings, don't mask them with broad\n   `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks.\n5. **Type safety** — No universe mismatches, coercion problems.\n6. **Performance** — Avoid expensive tactics on large types.\n7. **Modularity** — Are new lemmas general enough to be reused?\n8. **Documentation** — Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.\n9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** — Add `\\lean{}` and `\\leanok` tags for\n   formalized statements only when the Lean statement matches the source.\n   Record formalization-only auxiliary lemmas explicitly.\n10. **Scaffolding integrity** — Verify scaffolding aligns with Mathlib.\n11. **Statement drift** — Compare source-labelled theorem statements with the\n   paper and flag new hypotheses, weakened conclusions, changed quantifier\n   order, altered error parameters, or bridge/residual packages moving toward\n   a paper theorem.\n12. **Proof-evasion anti-patterns** — Review against `docs/anti_patterns.md`.\n\nFor full details, see `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` and the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review` reference.\n\n## Blueprint and Documentation Work\n\nIf modifying blueprint material:\n\n- Keep chapter structure under `blueprint/src/chapter/`\n- Ensure `leanblueprint web` succeeds\n- Keep Lean declaration references valid\n- Sync theorem Section 6: main induction wrapper\\\\n\\\\nDo not start from the final theorem and guess intermediate facts.\\\\n\\\\n## Faithful Formalization Policy\\\\n\\\\nA declaration is a formalization of a paper theorem only when its public Lean\\\\nstatement matches the cited paper statement, up to faithful formal encoding.\\\\nChanging a Lean theorem away from the corresponding statement in\\\\n`references/ldt-paper/` is strongly discouraged and should occur only when a\\\\nfaithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical necessity requires it.\\\\nThis applies to every declaration advertised as a formalization of a paper\\\\nresult, not only to theorems currently undergoing repair. These lighter\\\\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\\\\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\\\\npaper hypotheses.\\\\n\\\\n## Code Conventions\\\\n\\\\n### Imports\\\\n\\\\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\\\\n- One import per line\\\\n- Follow existing local import style\\\\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\\\\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\\\\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\\\\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\\\\n\\\\n### File structure\\\\n\\\\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\\\\n\\\\n1. imports\\\\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\\\\n3. namespace / opens / variables\\\\n4. declarations\\\\n\\\\n### Formatting\\\\n\\\\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\\\\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\\\\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\\\\n  own line\\\\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\\\\n  theorem statement\\\\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\\\\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. # Title ... ## References ... -/`\\\\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\\\\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\\\\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\\\\n\\\\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\\\\\\\lean{...}`\\\\nand `\\\\\\\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\\\\n\\\\n## Proof Engineering\\\\n\\\\n### Search before proving\\\\n\\\\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\\\\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\\\\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\\\\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\\\\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\\\\n\\\\n### Mathlib integration\\\\n\\\\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\\\\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\\\\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\\\\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\\\\n\\\\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\\\\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\\\\n\\\\n### Validation ladder\\\\n\\\\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\\\\n2. `lake build`\\\\n\\\\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\\\\n\\\\n### Lean-specific advice\\\\n\\\\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\\\\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\\\\n  already in the repo\\\\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\\\\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\\\\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\\\\n\\\\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\\\\n\\\\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Branch claim — one writer per BRANCH, not merely per worktree
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A branch can be checked out in more than one worktree, and on 2026-09-12 an
# autofix loop and a prover ran on PR 342's branch at once; every meta wave then
# needed a `git stash push` preamble. The worktree lock cannot see that, so the
# claim is keyed on the branch and names its holder when it refuses.
# Read-only sessions are exempt: they write nothing, and a lane's own review
# step must not refuse against its own prover's claim.

safe_component() {
  printf '%s' "$1" | tr '/' '-' | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '-'
}

claim_branch() {
  # claim_branch <branch>
  local branch="$1"
  local dir owner="" holder_role="" holder_session=""
  dir="$LOCK_DIR/branch-$(safe_component "$branch").claim"
  mkdir -p "$LOCK_DIR"
  while ! mkdir "$dir" 2>/dev/null; do
    owner="$(cat "$dir/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -n "$owner" ] && ! kill -0 "$owner" 2>/dev/null; then
      note "breaking stale branch claim $dir (pid $owner is gone)"
      rm -rf "$dir"
      continue
    fi
    holder_role="$(cat "$dir/role" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    holder_session="$(cat "$dir/session" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    die 5 "branch '$branch' is claimed by session ${holder_session:-unknown} \
(role ${holder_role:-unknown}, pid ${owner:-unknown}).
  Two writers on one branch produce interleaved commits and a stash-and-hope
  recovery (events.md 2026-09-12, PR 342). Wait for that session, or pass
  --allow-concurrent if you have a reason and can name it."
  done
  printf '%s\n' "$$" >"$dir/pid"
  printf '%s\n' "$ROLE" >"$dir/role"
  printf '%s\n' "$NAME" >"$dir/session"
  date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z >"$dir/since"
  LOCKS_HELD[${#LOCKS_HELD[@]}]="$dir"
  BRANCH_CLAIM="$dir"
# One writer per worktree, one writer per branch
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

ACCOUNT_REQUESTED="$ACCOUNT"
resolve_cutoff

if [ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 0 ] && [ "$SANDBOX" != "read-only" ]; then
  WT_KEY="$(printf '%s' "$WORKTREE_ABS" | cksum | tr -d ' ' | cut -c1-12)"
  WT_BASE="$(printf '%s' "$(basename "$WORKTREE_ABS")" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '-')"
  acquire_lock "worktree-$WT_BASE-$WT_KEY" "$LOCK_WAIT" "worktree $WORKTREE_ABS"
fi

BRANCH="$(git -C "$WORKTREE_ABS" symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ "$SANDBOX" = "read-only" ]; then
  : # a reader writes nothing, and must not refuse against its own lane's prover
elif [ "$ALLOW_CONCURRENT" -eq 1 ]; then
  note "--allow-concurrent: not claiming branch '${BRANCH:-<detached>}'; say why in events.md"
elif [ -z "$BRANCH" ]; then
  note "worktree $WORKTREE_ABS has a detached HEAD; there is no branch to claim"
else
  claim_branch "$BRANCH"
fi

resolve_labels "$ACCOUNT_REQUESTED"

if [ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 0 ]; then
  SPOOL_FILE="$SPOOL_DIR/$NAME_BASE.json"
  SPOOL_PROMPT="$SPOOL_DIR/$NAME_BASE.prompt.txt"
  mkdir -p "$SPOOL_DIR"
  ( umask 077; cp "$PROMPT_FILE" "$SPOOL_PROMPT" ) ||
    die 4 "cannot write the spool prompt at $SPOOL_PROMPT"
  write_spool queued
fi

if [ -n "$CONTINUATION_JSON" ]; then
  # Validated once, before the loop: a transient-class retry must never consume
  # a proof packet attempt and never reset a budget.
  (umask 077; set -C; printf '%s\n' "$CONTINUATION_JSON" > "$CAPTURE_DIR/$NAME_BASE.continuation.json")
fi

#                         [--continue-from FILE]  fresh primary checkpoint/budget handoff JSON
